translations.title: Maintaining Your Identity
translations.explanation: Maintaining Your Identity is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Advanced Trigonometry & Geometry”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:HSF-TF.A.3, CCSS:HSF-TF.A.4. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: (+) Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent f or π/3, π/4 and π/6, and use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosine, and tangent for π–x, π+x, and 2π–x in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number. (+) Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions. Instructional focus: Students connect angle measure, the unit circle, right-triangle ratios, periodic behavior, and trigonometric identities. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Maintaining Your Identity. On the unit circle, cosine and sine give x- and y-coordinates. Radians connect angle measure with arc length. Trigonometric identities must be transformed through valid algebraic steps and domain conditions.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: In a right triangle with legs 9 and 4, the hypotenuse is √(9²+4²)≈9.849. For the angle opposite the side 9, sin θ≈0.914 and cos θ≈0.406. Example 2: In a right triangle with legs 3 and 8, the hypotenuse is √(3²+8²)≈8.544. For the angle opposite the side 3, sin θ≈0.351 and cos θ≈0.936.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: use the Pythagorean theorem: c=√(81+16)≈9.849. Step 2: relative to the chosen angle, opposite=9, adjacent=4. Step 3: sin θ=9/9.849≈0.914; cos θ=4/9.849≈0.406. Step 4: verify both ratios are between 0 and 1. Step 1: use the Pythagorean theorem: c=√(9+64)≈8.544. Step 2: relative to the chosen angle, opposite=3, adjacent=8. Step 3: sin θ=3/8.544≈0.351; cos θ=8/8.544≈0.936. Step 4: verify both ratios are between 0 and 1.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Maintaining Your Identity. Do not mix degrees and radians without conversion. Do not cancel trigonometric sums term by term. Check quadrant signs and domain restrictions.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Maintaining Your Identity. Identify the angle representation, use the appropriate triangle or unit-circle relationship, calculate, and check sign, period, and units.

translations.title: Cavelieri to the Rescue
translations.explanation: Cavelieri to the Rescue is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Advanced Trigonometry & Geometry”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:HSG-GMD.A.2. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: (+) Give an informal argument using Cavalieri’s principle for the formulas for the v olume of a sphere and other solid figures. Instructional focus: Students reason about area, volume, cross-sections, and dimensional relationships in two- and three-dimensional figures. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Cavelieri to the Rescue. Area uses square units and volume uses cubic units. Scaling all lengths by k scales area by k^2 and volume by k^3. Cross-sections depend on the plane cutting the solid.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: A cylinder with radius 4 and height 8 has volume V=πr²h=π(4²)(8)=128π cubic units, about 402.12. Example 2: A cylinder with radius 6 and height 6 has volume V=πr²h=π(6²)(6)=216π cubic units, about 678.58.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: identify radius r=4 and height h=8. Step 2: square the radius: 4²=16. Step 3: multiply by height: 16×8=128. Step 4: volume is 128π≈402.12 cubic units. Step 1: identify radius r=6 and height h=6. Step 2: square the radius: 6²=36. Step 3: multiply by height: 36×6=216. Step 4: volume is 216π≈678.58 cubic units.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Cavelieri to the Rescue. Do not use a surface-area formula when volume is requested. Track whether a dimension is radius or diameter and keep units consistent.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Cavelieri to the Rescue. Identify the geometric quantity and dimensions, apply the appropriate formula or scaling relationship, calculate, and state squared or cubed units correctly.

Główny kierunek pracy: Uczeń analizuje pola, objętości, przekroje i zależności wymiarowe figur dwu- i trójwymiarowych. translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Cel tej lekcji: Pomiar geometryczny i wymiar — Cavelieri to the Rescue. Pole wyraża się w jednostkach kwadratowych, a objętość w sześciennych. Skalowanie wszystkich długości przez k skaluje pole przez k^2, a objętość przez k^3. Przekrój zależy od płaszczyzny przecinającej bryłę.
translations.workedExamples: Przykład 1: Walec o promieniu 4 i wysokości 8 ma objętość V=πr²h=128π, czyli około 402.12 jednostek sześciennych. Przykład 2: Walec o promieniu 6 i wysokości 6 ma objętość V=πr²h=216π, czyli około 678.58 jednostek sześciennych.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: r=4, h=8. Krok 2: r²=16. Krok 3: 16×8=128. Krok 4: V=128π≈402.12 jednostek sześciennych. Krok 1: r=6, h=6. Krok 2: r²=36. Krok 3: 36×6=216. Krok 4: V=216π≈678.58 jednostek sześciennych.
translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Pomiar geometryczny i wymiar — Cavelieri to the Rescue. Nie używaj wzoru na pole powierzchni, gdy pytanie dotyczy objętości. Sprawdzaj, czy podana wielkość jest promieniem czy średnicą, i zachowuj spójne jednostki.
translations.quickSummary: Cel tej lekcji: Pomiar geometryczny i wymiar — Cavelieri to the Rescue. Rozpoznaj wielkość geometryczną i wymiary, zastosuj właściwy wzór lub skalowanie, oblicz i poprawnie zapisz jednostki kwadratowe lub sześcienne.

translations.title: Operating on a Shoestring
translations.explanation: Operating on a Shoestring is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Advanced Trigonometry & Geometry”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:HSG-GPE.A.3. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: (+) Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given the foci, using the fact tha t the sum or difference of distances from the foci is constant. Instructional focus: Students use coordinates and algebra to describe geometric objects, prove relationships, and calculate distances, slopes, and equations. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Operating on a Shoestring. Slope represents direction and rate of change. Parallel nonvertical lines have equal slopes; perpendicular nonvertical lines have slopes whose product is -1. Distance and midpoint formulas follow from coordinate differences.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: For A(1,1) and B(3,6), slope = (6-1)/(3-1) = 5/2. Example 2: For A(4,2) and B(6,8), slope = (8-2)/(6-4) = 3/1.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: y-change is 5=5. Step 2: x-change is 2=2. Step 3: slope is 5/2=5/2. Step 4: keep the subtraction order consistent for both coordinates. Step 1: y-change is 6=6. Step 2: x-change is 2=2. Step 3: slope is 6/2=3/1. Step 4: keep the subtraction order consistent for both coordinates.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Operating on a Shoestring. Do not divide by zero when a line is vertical. Keep x- and y-differences paired in the same order when calculating slope.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Operating on a Shoestring. Translate the geometry into coordinates, calculate the needed algebraic quantity, and interpret the result as a geometric property.
